```{r}
# Made-up data for this demo, don't reuse it thinking it's real.

pacman::p_load(rio, tidyverse)
```

# Wide to long and back

```{r}
wide <- import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx")

head(wide)
```

```{r}
# names_to and values_to are just what you want the two new columns called
# 93 rows turn into 744, same numbers just stacked
long <- wide %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = wk40:wk47, names_to = "week", values_to = "cases")

head(long, 12)
```

```{r}
# and back
long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = week, values_from = cases) %>%
  head()
```

# Why bother

```{r}
# ggplot wants x, y, and fill each as one column. the wide table has no week column
ggplot(long, aes(x = week, y = cases, fill = region)) +
  geom_col()
```

# Crosstab

```{r}
# which = picks the sheet. leave it off and you get the first one
linelist <- import("K:/R Study Group/Trenton/Ch12 Pivot/pivot_demo_data.xlsx", which = "flu_linelist")

head(linelist)
```

```{r}
# count then widen. without values_fill = 0 the empty cells come out NA
linelist %>%
  count(county, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```
